BiblicalUsage: Beth-Shittah means house of the acacia, and it is named once, in Judges 7:22, in the rout of Midian: the host fled to Beth-shittah, with Gideon's three hundred blowing their trumpets behind them. A grove town on the road the enemy ran, named only because they ran that way.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the flight to Beth-shittah shows what God does with three hundred trumpets: the enemy runs, and even the road they take is remembered.
